production.note: US model years 2004-2006. Start: Auto123's '2004 Dodge Ram SRT-10 Road Test' (Khatir Soltani, August 2004). Dodge's 2005 press kit adds the Quad Cab for 2005 (dodge-ram-srt10-2005-presskit). End: TrueCar lists a 2006 Ram SRT-10 Regular Cab (truecar-ram-srt10-2006, database); no Dodge page stating 2006 was the last year was opened.

body.note: Dodge 2005 spec sheet: 'Two-Seat Ultimate Performance Pickup' with a 6 ft 3 in box. The regular cab is the launch configuration (2004) and the standard car; a four-door Quad Cab with an automatic was added for 2005 (dodge-ram-srt10-2005-presskit).

displacementL.note: Dodge: 'Displacement 8.3L, (505 cu. in.)'. No opened page states a cc figure (Dodge's sheet gives only litres and cubic inches).

aspiration.note: Viper V-10; no forced induction is listed; inferred.

drivetrain.note: 'rear-wheel drive', Dana Super-60 rear axle, 4.56 ratio.

transmission.note: Dodge 2005 press kit: regular cab, 'T-56 six-speed manual transmission fitted with a Hurst shifter'; Quad Cab (2005-2006), 'automatic transmission—a super-duty four-speed'. Spec sheet: 'Six-speed overdrive with Hurst shifter mechanism and linkage' (dodge-ram-srt10-2005-regcab-specs).

powerHp.note: Dodge 2005 Ram SRT-10 specifications, ENGINE section of the regular-cab sheet (the Quad Cab has its own sheet, not opened). Quote: "Power (SAE net): 500 bhp (372 kW) @ 5600 rpm (60.4 bhp/liter)"; "Torque (SAE net): 525 lb.-ft. (712 N•m @ 4200 rpm". Same rating for 2004: Auto123 (Khatir Soltani), "Engine: 500 hp, 525 lb-ft, 8.3-L, 20-valve, OHV, V10" (auto123-ram-srt10-2004); the 2005 press kit calls it the '500-horsepower, Viper-powered Dodge Ram SRT-10' (dodge-ram-srt10-2005-presskit).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (manufacturer figure labelled an estimate). 2005 regular cab, six-speed manual. Quote (Dodge 2005 regular-cab specifications, DIMENSIONS AND CAPACITIES): "Curb Weight (estimated) 5,100 lbs." Because it is labelled estimated it does not count at weight step 1. KBB's 2005 Regular Cab SRT-10 page, "Curb Weight 5100 lbs." (kbb-ram-srt10-2005), copies this figure exactly and is not an independent source, so only one 2005 figure exists. Auto123 (Khatir Soltani, 2004 road test): "Curb Weight: 2,336 kg (5,150 lbs)" (auto123-ram-srt10-2004) is a 2004 figure. See discrepancies.

discrepancies.reason: Both Dodge figures are labelled estimates: 5,000 lb in the 2004 launch release ('Curb Weight (estimated): 5,000 lbs.', as reproduced by ROCKCRAWLER.com) and 5,100 lb in the 2005 regular-cab sheet. KBB copies each exactly (2004 5,000 lb, kbb-ram-srt10-2004; 2005 5,100 lb, kbb-ram-srt10-2005). Auto123's 2004 road test prints 5,150 lb. The figures span 3%, and none is a final manufacturer figure.
discrepancies.resolution: 5,100 lb used only because it is the figure for the 2005 reference year; it is not more final than 5,000 lb (both are Dodge estimates for different model years). A final Dodge curb weight or a major magazine's specification panel is needed.

provisionalNote: Weight (5,100 lb, 2005 regular cab) rests on Dodge's 2005 spec sheet, which labels it '(estimated)'; KBB repeats it exactly and is not independent, so only one 2005 figure exists. Dodge's 2004 launch estimate was 5,000 lb and Auto123's 2004 spec list 5,150 lb. A final (non-estimated) Dodge curb weight or a major magazine's specification panel would replace it. The 2006 end year rests on TrueCar listing a 2006 model.
